description: A responsive grid of recent Instagram posts fetched via an RSS-to-JSON bridge. Because Instagram's Basic Display API was deprecated in December 2024, this component consumes a JSON Feed v1 URL produced by a free service like rss.app or rsshub.app — the designer pastes in the generated feed URL and the component handles fetching, parsing, and rendering. Supports a configurable post count (up to 24), 2 / 3 / 4 column grid on desktop with responsive collapse on mobile, square / portrait / original aspect ratios, and one of four hover effects (none, zoom, overlay, fade). Each post shows the image, optional truncated caption, and optional relative date; clicking a post opens the original on instagram.com in a new tab. Includes a header with a profile link and a 'Follow on Instagram' CTA. Skeleton loading state, friendly error state with retry, and empty state when the feed is currently empty. Client-side cache keeps the quota-friendly request rate gentle.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML ID for targeting with CSS or JavaScript

props.name: feedUrl
props.description: JSON Feed URL from an RSS-to-JSON bridge. Generate one for any public Instagram account at rss.app (free tier) by pointing it at instagram.com/{handle} and copying the JSON URL. Must return JSON Feed v1 format.

props.name: profileUrl
props.description: Link to the Instagram profile (e.g. https://www.instagram.com/yourhandle/)

props.name: heading
props.description: Optional heading above the feed

props.name: subheading
props.description: Optional subheading below the heading

props.name: showHeading
props.description: Show or hide the heading block

props.name: followButtonText
props.description: Text on the 'Follow on Instagram' CTA

props.name: showFollowButton
props.description: Show or hide the follow CTA in the header

props.name: maxPosts
props.description: Maximum number of posts to display (1–24)

props.name: refreshInterval
props.description: Client-side cache duration in minutes (0 disables caching)

props.name: openInNewTab
props.description: Open posts on instagram.com in a new browser tab

props.name: columns
props.description: Number of columns on desktop (collapses responsively on narrow screens)

props.name: aspectRatio
props.description: Aspect ratio of each post tile

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between post tiles in pixels

props.name: hoverEffect
props.description: Hover treatment on post tiles

props.name: borderRadius
props.description: Corner rounding on post tiles

props.name: showCaption
props.description: Show the post caption below each tile (uses overlay on hover when hoverEffect='overlay')

props.name: captionLines
props.description: Maximum number of caption lines before truncating with an ellipsis

props.name: showDate
props.description: Show the relative post date (e.g. '3 days ago')

props.name: loadingText
props.description: Text shown while the feed is loading

props.name: errorText
props.description: Message shown when the feed fails to load
props.defaultValue: We couldn't reach Instagram right now. Please try again in a moment.

props.name: retryButtonText
props.description: Text on the retry button

props.name: emptyStateText
props.description: Message shown when the feed is empty

apiIntegrations.service: JSON Feed v1 via rss.app or rsshub.app (Instagram bridge)
apiIntegrations.notes:
IMPORTANT — IG's own Basic Display API was deprecated on 2024-12-04, so this component deliberately does NOT call graph.instagram.com. Instead it accepts any JSON Feed v1 URL from a third-party bridge; rss.app is the recommended free option because it produces a stable schema and handles IG's auth on its own backend.

FIELD FALLBACKS: different bridges populate different fields. Always resolve the image URL with a chain like: item.image || item.banner_image || item.attachments?.find(a => a.mime_type?.startsWith('image/'))?.url. Always resolve the caption with: item.content_text || item.title || '' (bridges sometimes stuff the caption into the title).

CAPTION CLEANUP: Instagram captions often include newlines and hashtags; respect the captionLines prop by applying CSS line-clamp, don't pre-truncate in JS.

REELS & CAROUSELS: bridges represent video reels with a video mime type in attachments. For this component, just show the still thumbnail from item.image and link to the instagram.com URL; the user will see the video when they click through.

CORS: rss.app serves JSON feeds with permissive CORS headers; rsshub.app is the same. If a user plugs in a custom feed and hits CORS errors, the error state copy should point them toward rss.app.

RATE LIMITS: rss.app caches its own fetch against IG (usually 15-minute windows). Combine that with the refreshInterval prop on the client so we only re-fetch the JSON feed once per interval.
